question: How many crimes under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 now include increased imprisonment terms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**33 crimes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023** is proposed to replace the Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860 as part of comprehensive legal reforms in India.
 
• The new legal framework includes increased imprisonment terms for **33 specific crimes**, reflecting the evolving nature of criminal activities and a focus on stricter punishments.
 
• These changes aim to address issues like **cybercrime, organized crime, sexual offenses, and crimes against women and children**, which have become more prevalent in the modern era.
 
• The reforms also emphasize improving the efficiency of the criminal justice system and ensuring quicker resolution of cases through updated legal provisions.
 
• By increasing the punishment for these crimes, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita aims to serve as a deterrent to criminal activity and ensure better protection for citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:**

 
 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita focuses on **simplifying the legal language** and addressing ambiguities in the earlier Indian Penal Code (IPC).
 
• It introduces provisions for **new-age crimes**, such as cybercrimes, while retaining the core principles of the IPC.
 
• Provisions for enhanced punishment terms aim to ensure justice for victims and act as a deterrent for offenders.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Crimes with Increased Imprisonment:**
 
 
• Stronger penalties for **sexual offenses**, including crimes against women and children.
 
• Enhanced sentences for **cybercrimes**, considering the rise in online fraud and misuse of technology.
 
• Increased imprisonment for **organized crimes**, such as human trafficking and drug smuggling.
 
 
 
• **Legal Reforms and Modernization:**
 
 
• The new legislation aligns with **global standards**, ensuring that India's legal framework is equipped to handle contemporary challenges.
 
• It emphasizes the use of **technology** in judicial processes, including digital evidence and case management systems.
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Criminal Justice System:**
 
 
• The changes are expected to improve the efficiency and credibility of the Indian judicial system.
 
• By addressing modern-day crimes, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita aims to ensure **better protection of citizens' rights**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Indian Penal Code (IPC) was enacted in **1860** during British colonial rule and served as the foundation of India's criminal law system.
 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, represents a significant **modernization** of this century-old legal framework.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Law Commission:**
 
 
• The reforms were proposed after extensive consultations and recommendations by the **Law Commission of India**.
 
• The aim was to create a more **citizen-friendly legal system** that reflects the aspirations of a contemporary society.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, will come into effect after approval from the Indian Parliament and Presidential assent.
 
• It will replace the IPC, marking a **historic shift** in India's legal landscape.
